## 1. Summary

PathSnap converts a noisy GPS track into the sequence of road segments (arcs) a vehicle drove. Our pipeline has four stages:
(1) **candidate generation**: every GPS point gets up to 25 road arcs within 60 m; (2) a **classifier** (HistGradientBoosting on 23 features)
scores how likely each candidate is the true arc; (3) an **HMM/Viterbi decoder** chooses the most coherent arc sequence through the road
network; (4) a **FastAPI** server returns the predicted route to a UI running on a second laptop and scores it server-side against private reference routes.

| Result (pointwise accuracy on points whose true arc is among the candidates; mean over trips) | Training trips (out-of-fold) | Student-test trips |
|---|---|---|
| Classifier only | {{hmm.train_oof.classifier_only.acc_covered:pct}}% | {{hmm.student_test.classifier_only.acc_covered:pct}}% |
| Classifier + tuned HMM (**final system**) | **{{hmm.train_oof.hmm_tuned.acc_covered:pct}}%** | **{{hmm.student_test.hmm_tuned.acc_covered:pct}}%** |
| Route continuity, final system | {{hmm.train_oof.hmm_tuned.continuity:.3f}} | {{hmm.student_test.hmm_tuned.continuity:.3f}} |

Key findings (all measured, see Sections 3-5):

- **The HMM decoder adds the most.** Over classifier-only top-1 it adds {{gain.hmm_train:.1f}} accuracy points on the training trips (out-of-fold) and {{gain.hmm_student:.1f}} points on the student-test trips.
- **Neighbour-point context features lift the classifier.** Classifier-only top-1 rises by {{gain.feat_clf_train:.1f}} points (training, out-of-fold); after HMM decoding the final system is {{gain.feat_final_train:.1f}} points (training) and {{gain.feat_final_student:.1f}} points (student-test) better than the 11-feature system.
- **Bayesian tuning of the classifier barely matters.** Cross-validation macro-F1 changes by {{gain.tune_cv:+.4f}} ({{m.hgb_base.cv_macro_f1:.4f}} to {{m.hgb_tuned.cv_macro_f1:.4f}}), which is within fold-to-fold variation (Section 4).
- **Limits.** The reference route has no per-point labels, so "pointwise accuracy" uses labels derived by aligning each GPS point to the ordered reference route; two training trips (00000033, 00000054) have a constant 130-140 m offset between GPS and reference; the student-test set has only 10 trips (Sections 2 and 5).
